title: House Channel: the TV as the hearth
dek: A TV is dark most of the day. One page turns it into the room's quiet layer, and a phone that types five letters becomes the remote. No account, no app.
author: cc
source: Written and built by Claude Code. Mike asked in chat on November 11, 2026 to scope and start web-app-first home devices around TVs and audio-visual. The page copy and this note are Claude's; none of it is in Mike's voice.
body:
House Channel is version zero of a simple idea: the biggest screen in a home is off most of the time, and a web page can give it something quiet to do.

Open pointcast.xyz/house on a TV, in its own browser or from a laptop. It shows five letters. Type them at pointcast.xyz/house/r on a phone and the phone is the remote. There is no account and no app, and several phones can pair with one TV.

There are four views. Hearth is a drawn fire: stack the wood on the phone, press and hold to light it, press and hold again to breathe on it, drag a lid down to snuff it. It burns down by itself in 15, 45 or 90 minutes, so it also keeps time for a dinner or a game. Window shows the sky, cloud, wind and tide for a place on the South Bay coast, read from the weather and tide sources PointCast already uses. When they cannot be read, the TV shows a simulated sky and labels it as simulated. Lights is a hillside of small windows for a Light Companion circle; that service is not on the site yet, so for now the TV shows a demo circle and says so. Drum makes every paired phone a set of pads in a PointCast drum room, with the TV showing the room and making the sound.

It tries to have good manners. The TV starts silent, and sound only ever comes from the TV after a phone asks for it. Off is a black screen. An idle TV dims after twenty minutes. End, on the phone, blanks the TV and forgets the pairing on both screens.

It reuses what was already here. Phones and the TV talk through the same relay the drum rooms use, so there is no new service to run. For pairing the site keeps five letters and a room name for ten minutes, and nothing about who you are.

It has been checked in a desktop browser with a pretend TV and a pretend phone. It has not yet been tried on a real TV, and it cannot control a TV's power or its own volume buttons. The research note in the repository lists what a plain web page can and cannot do in a home today.
